topics.label: Atoms
facts: Atoms are the tiny building blocks that make up all matter.
An atom has a nucleus in the middle, made of protons and neutrons, with electrons moving around it.
Protons have a positive charge, electrons have a negative charge, and neutrons have no charge.
Different elements have different numbers of protons: hydrogen has one, and oxygen has eight.

choices: The tiny building block of all matter
questions.fact: Everything around you is made of atoms, far too small to see.

questions.q: What is in the middle of an atom?
choices: A nucleus made of protons and neutrons
questions.fact: The nucleus sits at the centre of the atom, with electrons moving around it.

questions.q: Which particle in an atom has a negative charge?
questions.fact: Electrons carry a negative charge, while protons are positive and neutrons are neutral.

questions.q: How many protons does a hydrogen atom have?
questions.fact: Hydrogen, the simplest element, has just one proton in its nucleus.

topics.label: Chemical Reactions
facts: A chemical reaction happens when substances change into new substances.
In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged but never created or destroyed.
Burning, rusting, and cooking are all chemical reactions.
Some reactions give out heat, like burning wood, and some take in heat, like baking a cake.

questions.q: What happens in a chemical reaction?
questions.fact: In a chemical reaction, atoms join together in new ways to make new substances.

questions.q: What happens to atoms during a chemical reaction?
choices: They are rearranged, never created or destroyed
questions.fact: Atoms are conserved in a reaction: the same atoms exist before and after, just joined differently.

questions.q: Which of these is a chemical reaction?
questions.fact: Rusting makes a new substance, iron oxide, while melting and dissolving are physical changes.

questions.q: What does burning wood give out?
questions.fact: Burning is a reaction that releases heat and light.

topics.label: The Periodic Table
facts: The periodic table organises all the known elements in order of their atomic number.
Elements in the same column, called a group, often behave in similar ways.
Hydrogen, oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen are some of the most important elements for life.
Gold, silver, and iron are elements that are metals, while oxygen and helium are gases.

questions.q: What does the periodic table organise?
questions.fact: The periodic table lists every known element, from hydrogen to the heaviest made in labs.

questions.q: What are elements in the same column of the periodic table called?
questions.fact: Elements in the same group share similar chemical behaviour.

questions.q: Which of these is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.fact: Gold's symbol is Au, from its Latin name aurum. Ag is silver.

questions.q: Which of these elements is a gas at room temperature?
questions.fact: Oxygen is a gas, while iron, gold, and copper are metals that are solid at room temperature.

topics.label: Acids and Bases
facts: An acid is a substance that can donate hydrogen ions, and lemon juice and vinegar are common acids.
A base, also called an alkali when it dissolves in water, can neutralise an acid.
The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, and above 7 is basic.
Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7.

questions.q: Which of these is an acid?
What can a base do to an acid?
questions.fact: A base reacts with an acid to neutralise it, often making a salt and water.

questions.q: What is the pH of a neutral substance?
questions.fact: On the pH scale, 7 is neutral, like pure water.
Values below 7 on the pH scale are acidic.
